objective: Let the shop keep its catalogue in several files (the main list, a supplier list, a seasonal list). `stockroom/csvio.py` gets `merge_catalogues(texts: Sequence[str]) -> list[Item]`, which reads each text with `read_items` (a read error of any file propagates unchanged, as the same `ParseError`) and returns one `Item` per SKU. The SKUs come in the order they first appear: the files in the given order, the rows of each file in file order; a file with only the header contributes nothing. A SKU may have several rows, in one file or in different files; rows that give the same record (equal `Item` values: same SKU, name, price, tags in the same order and reorder level) are simply kept once. An empty sequence of texts raises `ValueError`. Every command option that names a catalogue file may now be given more than once: `items --file`, `stock --items` and `price --items` (argparse `action="append"`, still required). The command then works on `merge_catalogues` of all the files given, in the order given: `items` lists the merged catalogue in the merged order with the existing table format, and `--tag` filters the merged list; `stock` checks the merged items against the stock file and reports them in the merged order; `price` looks the SKU up in the merged catalogue. With a single file the commands behave as before for catalogues without repeated SKUs. A read error in any of the files is a data error (exit code 1, nothing on stdout, `stockroom: error: MESSAGE` on stderr). The order file and the stock file are unchanged.
acceptance: `merge_catalogues` returns one item per SKU in order of first appearance across the files in the given order, equals `read_items` for a single file without repeated SKUs, ignores header-only files and raises `ValueError` for no texts
Rows that give equal `Item` values are kept once, whether they repeat inside one file or across files
A read error of any file propagates as the same `ParseError` (e.g. `item header must be sku,name,price,tags,reorder_level`)

`items --file A --file B`, `stock --items A --items B --stock S` and `price --items A --items B ...` use the merged catalogue (listing order, `--tag` after merging, low-stock lines in merged order, price lookup), and a bad file exits with 1, nothing on stdout and `stockroom: error: MESSAGE` on stderr

When several rows give one SKU, the merged catalogue holds exactly one item for it at the position where the SKU first appeared, and `items`, `stock` and `price` all use that same item (checked over many seeded random catalogues and in the commands)

interpretations: When rows for one SKU differ, the record read last (the later file, or the later row of one file) replaces the earlier one, keeping the position where the SKU first appeared
When rows for one SKU differ, the record read first is kept and later different rows are ignored
